verdict.rationale: Pandoc's primary first-party product is a standalone command-line program. The manual documents its flags, format selection, stdin/stdout piping and format listing, and it installs via Homebrew, Chocolatey and GitHub Actions. A community user describes scripted automation built on it, which supports its fit for programmatic and agent-driven use. Missing for 10: no evidence of agent-oriented affordances such as documented machine-readable/structured CLI output or an LLM-friendly docs format (llms.txt and markdown docs both 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Pandoc includes a Haskell library and a standalone command-line program.
If no input-files are specified, input is read from stdin. Output goes to stdout by default.
The input format can be specified using the -f/--from option, the output format using the -t/--to option.
You can also use pandoc --list-input-formats and pandoc --list-output-formats to print lists of supported formats.
Alternatively, you can install pandoc using Homebrew: brew install pandoc
Pandoc can be run through GitHub Actions.
scripts wrote model inputs as Markdown tables embedded in a Markdown writeup, and Pandoc produced the Word report for sponsors
